economic.note: In 2024 Maldives received about 4.0 tourist arrivals for every resident counted in Census 2022. Merchandise imports were about 39.8 times merchandise exports, while public and publicly guaranteed debt stood at 133.1% of GDP at end-2025. Together, these indicators show a highly connected economy that is also exposed to tourism, trade and financing shocks.

environment.tag: A tiny, low-lying land base inside a vast ocean territory
environment.strap: Very little land, an enormous EEZ and direct exposure of settlements and infrastructure to coastal hazards.
environment.compareStory: Maldives has only about 300 km² of land but an Exclusive Economic Zone of 859,000 km². It is physically tiny on land but enormous as an ocean state — a defining feature of its economy, geography and vulnerability.

environment.note: Environment at a glance: more than 80% of Maldives’ land is less than one metre above mean sea level, and more than 60% of inhabited islands face severe beach erosion. Government climate reporting also notes that 47% of housing structures — representing 42% of the population — are within 100 metres of the shore. This means climate and coastal risk directly affects homes, infrastructure, tourism and public finances.
